statement: In Washington you may file a name change petition in any district court in the state. In some instances it is filed in superior court instead — see RCW 4.24.130 to determine which court applies to your situation.
detail: Generally you complete a Petition for Name Change and an Order for Name Change. The Washington Courts website does not publish these forms. You have to contact the court you are filing in to get them, and the court directory lists every county court. Once the petition is done, a judge reviews it and signs it.

cost.note: Fees vary by county, and may also depend on how many people are named on the petition. Contact the court you are filing in for the exact fee.

statement: To change the name on your Washington driver's license or ID, make an appointment at a driver licensing office and bring a document that proves the name change, such as a court order filed and certified by the court.
detail: You pay the fee for a new license with the updated information, and a new photo is taken at the appointment. If you have a sealed name change order from a Washington superior court, the Department of Licensing asks you to contact its Identity Management Team instead. It says it follows a special process for sealed name changes to protect your privacy.

statement: Washington offers three gender designations on a driver's license or ID: M (male), F (female), and X (not exclusively male or female). You can change yours in person or by mail; there is no online option.
detail: In person, you bring your current card to a driver licensing office and confirm your gender designation out loud. By mail, you complete a Change of Gender Designation request form and mail it to the address on the form. The page does not ask for any medical documentation.

cost.note: If the gender designation is the only thing you update, the new card is free. If you update anything else at the same time, such as your name, there may be an extra fee.

statement: People who were born in Washington state can change the sex designation on their birth certificate by sending a completed request form to the state health department. A Washington birth certificate has three options: M, F, and X.
detail: Adults use the Request to Change Sex Designation on a Birth Certificate for an Adult (form DOH 422-143) and sign it in front of a notary. A court order or a letter from your physician will not be accepted. You do not get a new certificate on your own: to get one, send in the birth certificate order form as well.

cost.note: There is no fee to amend the record. A certified copy of the new birth certificate costs $25 each.

timeline.typical: about 3 business days to process, plus up to 2 weeks for mail

source.title: Washington State Department of Health — Sex Designation Change on a Birth Certificate

statement: Washington only changes the names on birth certificates for people who were born in Washington State. To change yours after a court-ordered name change, send a certified copy of the court order with the Court Order Legal Name Change Request (form DOH 422-126).
detail: The certified copy of the court order will not be returned to you, and photocopies are not accepted. A certified copy of the new birth certificate costs $25. The health department says it currently has a two (2) month processing turnaround time.

source.title: Washington State Department of Health — Court-Ordered Name Change on a Birth Certificate

topic: Washington name change for a minor child
statement: Washington law lets a person ask for a name change for their own child, the same way they can ask for their own name change. RCW 4.24.130 does not use the word "parent" for who may ask on a child's behalf — it says any person desiring a change of the person's name or that of the person's child may apply to the court.
detail: If the reason for a child's name change is related to gender expression or identity, the law sends the petition to superior court instead of district court, and once the court grants the name change it must seal the file to protect the child's privacy. After that, the file is not open to public inspection except by court order for good cause, or at the request of the person whose name was changed or their guardian. The statute does not say whether both parents must join the petition, does not say a non-petitioning parent must be given notice, and does not set an age at which a child's own consent matters — it is silent on all three. It also does not use a "best interest of the child" standard.

topic: Washington birth certificate sex designation for a minor
statement: Washington has a separate form for a minor's sex-designation change on a birth certificate: the Request to Change Sex Designation on a Birth Certificate for a Minor (form DOH 422-144). A parent or legal guardian must complete and sign it on behalf of a minor under 18, and it must also be signed by a licensed health care or mental health care provider who determines the change is consistent with the minor's identity.
detail: A legal guardian signing on the minor's behalf must include proof of legal guardianship, such as a certified court order, and a copy of their own government-issued photo ID. This is different from the adult path: adults sign for themselves in front of a notary, and no health-care-provider signature is required for an adult. An emancipated minor uses the adult form (DOH 422-143) instead, and must include proof of legal emancipation. If the minor has not legally changed their first and middle names, those can be changed on the same form with the consent of all listed parents; if the minor's name has already been legally changed, a certified court order must be included.

source.title: Washington State Department of Health — Sex Designation Change on a Birth Certificate

topic: Washington driver's license or permit gender designation for a minor
statement: Washington's gender-designation-change process names no different rule for someone under 18. The Department of Licensing page and its Change of Gender Designation request form cover an instruction permit — the credential most minors hold — the same way they cover a full driver's license or ID card.
detail: The request form has a single signature line, for the applicant themselves, declaring under penalty of perjury that they are the person named on the form. It does not have a separate line for a parent's or guardian's signature, and neither the department's page nor the form mentions age, being under 18, or any parent/guardian role in this process.
